summary: @or-sdk/web-search preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package's `preinstall` script runs `node setup.mjs` at `npm install`. `setup.mjs` is itself obfuscated with obfuscator.io-style hex-renamed identifiers and per-function encoded string dictionaries that hide calls including `execFileSync('ldd', ['--version'],...)` and `readFileSync('/etc/os-release', 'utf8')` (host reconnaissance). If `bun` is not present on PATH, the loader downloads a Bun release archive from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<V>/<arch>.zip`, extracts the binary to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync(bunPath, [path.join(D, 'math_init.js')], { stdio: 'inherit', cwd: D })`. The invoked `math_init.js` is a 727 KB Bun-compiled file (header `// @bun @bun-cjs`) with string-array-shuffle obfuscation (constant table `n7gIxM=[...]` and rotator `WV8StW`) whose behavior is opaque to review. The package is advertised as a WebSearch client, a purpose that has no need to fetch a second language runtime at install time to execute a bundled, obfuscated JS file. The alternate-runtime-dropper shape exists specifically to execute code under an interpreter that Node-focused scanners do not inspect, and the obfuscation of both the loader and the payload is consistent with anti-analysis rather than legitimate build tooling.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
